references.name: Walter Bagehot
Hyman P. Minsky
references.desc:
John Maynard Keynes (1975) and
the Financial Instability Hypothesis
references.connection:
The theoretical backbone; Minsky’s model
structures every chapter

references.name: Charles Mackay
references.desc:
Extraordinary Popular Delusions and
the Madness of Crowds (1841)
references.connection:
Classic account of tulipmania and the South Sea
Bubble; Kindleberger both draws on and corrects
Mackay

references.name: Milton Friedman & Anna Schwartz
references.desc:
A Monetary History of the United
States (1963)
references.connection:
The monetarist counter-narrative; Kindleberger
engages with their interpretation of the Great
Depression throughout

references.name: Joseph Schumpeter
references.connection:
Theory of creative destruction and the role of
innovation in driving economic cycles; provides
the concept of displacement

references.name: Adam Smith
references.connection:
Referenced for his analysis of overtrading and
the observation that speculation follows easy
credit

references.name: Irving Fisher
references.connection:
Mechanism by which falling prices increase real
debt burdens, creating a self-reinforcing
downward spiral

references.name: John Clapham
references.desc:
The Bank of England: A History
(1945)
references.connection:
Definitive institutional history; Kindleberger
draws on it extensively for British crisis
episodes

references.name: O.M.W. Sprague
references.desc:
History of Crises Under the National
Banking System (1910)

references.name: R.G. Hawtrey
references.connection:
Analysis of 1931; the argument that
international credits must be unlimited or
they are wasted

references.name: Fernand Braudel
references.connection:
The longue durée approach to
economic history; influenced Kindleberger’s
method of studying centuries-long patterns

references.name: H.M. Hyndman
references.desc:
Commercial Crises of the Nineteenth
Century (1892)
references.connection:
Historical detail on 19th-century financial
crises from a socialist perspective
